title: From Silk to Glass: The Caravan Exchange That Shaped the World
title_zh: 从丝绸到玻璃：重塑世界的商队贸易
intro_zh: 本文约900词，适合CET-4水平，核心词汇约6个，句子难度适中。

paragraphs.en: When people think of the ancient Silk Road, they often picture caravans loaded with valuable Chinese silk. But this legendary trade network carried far more than glossy cloth. It was a bridge between East and West, moving goods, ideas, and even diseases. For more than a thousand years, it connected the great empires of Han China, Parthia, and Rome. The two desires for silk and glass led to a lively exchange of luxury goods. These products shaped economies and connected distant cultures. The Silk Road, in fact, was not a single road but a web of routes stretching over 7,000 kilometers from China to the Mediterranean Sea.
paragraphs.zh: 当人们想到古代丝绸之路时，脑海中常会浮现满载贵重中国丝绸的商队。但这条传奇的贸易网络运输的远不止华丽布料。它是一座连接东西方的桥梁，不仅运输商品，还传播思想和疾病。一千多年来，它连接了汉帝国、帕提亚和罗马等伟大帝国。对丝绸和玻璃的追求引发了活跃的奢侈品交流。这些商品塑造了经济，联结了遥远的文化。事实上，丝绸之路并非一条单一道路，而是一个从中国延伸到地中海、总长超过7000公里的路线网。

paragraphs.en: Silk was the engine that started it all. For centuries, China kept the secret of sericulture, the art of raising silkworms and weaving their cocoons into fine thread. In the imperial workshops, thousands of women worked to produce the finest bolts. A single bolt of silk could buy a man's freedom or a general's loyalty. Its value was so high that in ancient Rome, silk was weighed against gold. Because of this demand, silk became the primary commodity of the Silk Road, and the trade route itself was named after it. But silk alone did not make the route truly global. The road also carried wool, jade, horses, and spices from Central Asia, as well as precious metals. For example, the Chinese prized the famous 'heavenly horses' of Fergana.
paragraphs.zh: 丝绸是启动这一切的引擎。几个世纪以来，中国一直保守着养蚕术的秘密，即饲养蚕虫并将其茧抽成细丝的艺术。在皇家工坊中，成千上万的妇女劳动，生产出最精美的绸缎。一匹丝绸可以买下一个人的自由，或赢得一位将军的忠诚。它的价值如此之高，在古罗马，丝绸被放在天平上与黄金对等。由于这种需求，丝绸成为丝绸之路的主要商品，整个贸易路线也因此得名。但丝绸本身并没有让这条路真正全球化。商路还运送来自中亚的羊毛、玉石、马匹和香料，以及贵金属。例如，中国人珍爱大宛的名马"天马"。

paragraphs.en: The opening of the Silk Road is often credited to a Chinese envoy named Zhang Qian. Around 138 BCE, the Han emperor sent him westward to form alliances, and though he failed in his diplomatic mission, he returned with detailed reports of strange lands and riches. His journeys revealed that trade with Central Asia could be profitable and secure. Over time, Chinese rulers encouraged merchants to follow his path. Eventually, private traders, not governments, brought the route to life. They organized large caravans that could include hundreds of camels, each loaded with silk, bronze mirrors, or lacquerware to the West. In return, they brought back horses, grapes, alfalfa, and even new musical instruments. These caravans were the lifeline of the Silk Road, and they operated on a schedule that could take a year or more for a one-way trip.
paragraphs.zh: 丝绸之路的开辟通常归功于中国使节张骞。公元前138年左右，汉朝皇帝派他西行结盟。虽然他的外交使命失败了，但他带回了关于异域和财富的详细报告。他的经历表明，与中亚的贸易既有利可图又安全。随着时间的推移，中国统治者鼓励商人沿他的足迹前行。最终，不是政府，而是私人商人使这条路线活跃起来。他们组织起庞大的商队，有时包括数百头骆驼，满载丝绸、铜镜和漆器运往西方。作为回报，他们带回马匹、葡萄、苜蓿，甚至新的乐器。这些商队是丝绸之路的生命线，它们的行程往往单向就需要一年或更长时间。

paragraphs.en: Life on the road was harsh. Caravans had to cross deserts that were scorching by day and freezing at night. Water was scarce, and sandstorms could swallow a whole line of beasts. Merchants also faced the constant threat of bandits. Yet they pressed on, because the potential profit was enormous. To survive, they traveled in groups, moved at night, and used landmarks to navigate. The most famous route ran from Chang'an through the Hexi Corridor, crossed the Taklamakan Desert, and then split into northern and southern paths before meeting again at Kashgar. The landscape was often desolate, with no villages for days. Caravan leaders had to calculate exactly how much food and water each animal needed, and a single mistake could mean disaster.
paragraphs.zh: 旅途生活十分艰苦。商队必须穿越白天灼热、夜晚严寒的沙漠。水十分稀缺，沙暴可以吞噬一整队牲畜。商人还经常面临盗贼的威胁。然而他们继续前行，因为潜在利润巨大。为了生存，他们结伴而行，在夜间赶路，利用地标导航。最著名的路线从长安出发，经河西走廊，穿越塔克拉玛干沙漠，然后分成南北两条支线，最后在喀什汇合。沿途景观往往荒凉，数日不见村庄。商队首领必须精确计算每头牲畜所需的食物和水，一个失误就可能导致灾难。

paragraphs.en: While silk flowed west, glass traveled east. The Roman Empire was famous for its glassmaking, producing transparent bowls and colored jewelry that astonished the Chinese. In fact, Chinese records from the 1st century CE mention 'sea-mud glass' from distant lands. Because the secret of making clear glass was unknown in China for a long time, imported glass was considered more precious than gold or gems. After seeing these exquisite objects, Chinese artisans began to experiment and eventually learned to imitate Roman techniques. But they did not copy them exactly. Instead, they developed new styles, such as the famous 'glazed pottery' that later influenced ceramics across Asia. This is a perfect example of how the Silk Road did more than move objects – it transferred skills and inspired innovation.
paragraphs.zh: 当丝绸流向西方时，玻璃则向东传播。罗马帝国以玻璃制造闻名，生产出令中国人惊叹的透明碗和彩色珠宝。事实上，公元1世纪的中国文献提到了来自遥远国度的"海泥玻璃"。由于中国长时间不清楚制造透明玻璃的方法，进口玻璃被视为比黄金和宝石更珍贵。看到这些精美器物后，中国工匠开始尝试，最终学会了模仿罗马技术。但他们并非完全照搬，而是发展出新的风格，例如后来影响亚洲陶瓷业的著名"釉陶"。这完美地说明了丝绸之路不仅仅是运送物品，还传播了技艺，激发了创新。

paragraphs.en: Beyond silk and glass, the most valuable shipment moving along the Silk Road may have been knowledge. Paper, invented in China, reached the Arab world and then Europe, changing how people recorded and shared information. Along the way, merchants carried mathematical ideas, astronomical knowledge, and medical treatments. The spread of Buddhism from India to China via these routes is another powerful example. The famous Dunhuang caves contain murals and manuscripts that tell of traders and pilgrims meeting in oasis towns. One vivid story tells of a Sogdian merchant named Miwnay, whose letters from the 4th century CE describe a network of contacts stretching from Central Asia to China. These letters are among the earliest personal records of trade on the route. They also show that even small-scale merchants could survive by adapting to many different cultures.
paragraphs.zh: 除了丝绸和玻璃，丝绸之路沿途最珍贵的货物也许是知识。中国发明的纸张传到阿拉伯世界，再传入欧洲，改变了人们记录和分享信息的方式。一路上，商人传播数学思想、天文知识和医疗方法。佛教通过这条路从印度传到中国，又是一个有力的例子。著名敦煌石窟中的壁画和手稿讲述了商人和朝圣者在绿洲城镇相遇的故事。其中一个生动的故事讲述了一位名为米奈的粟特商人，他4世纪的书信描述了从中亚延伸到中国的庞大联系网络。这些信件是丝绸之路上最早的私人贸易记录之一。它们还表明，即使是小商贩也能通过适应多种文化而生存。

paragraphs.en: The cities on the Silk Road were where all these exchanges came together. Samarkand, Bukhara, and Dunhuang became melting pots of culture and commerce. A typical bazaar in Samarkand might sell Chinese silk, Roman glass, Indian spices, and local melons side by side. The merchants themselves were often multilingual, moving easily between markets. They relied on trust and shared customs. One fifteenth-century caravan leader is said to have kept a ledger of dozens of transactions, recording prices for pepper, textiles, and jade. Such records show that trade was not just about luxury; it also included everyday goods. The constant flow of people made these cities tremendously wealthy and open to new ideas. For instance, Samarkand grew to be one of the largest cities in Central Asia, with a population of over a hundred thousand at its peak.
paragraphs.zh: 丝绸之路上的城市是所有这些交流交汇的地方。撒马尔罕、布哈拉和敦煌成为文化和商业的大熔炉。在撒马尔罕的典型市集上，中国丝绸、罗马玻璃、印度香料和当地甜瓜可能并排出售。商人本身通常通晓多种语言，在不同市场间自如穿梭。他们依靠信任和共享的习俗。据说，一位15世纪的商队首领保存着一本账本，记录了数十笔交易，包括胡椒、纺织品和玉石的价格。这些记录表明，贸易不仅涉及奢侈品，还包括日常商品。不断流动的人口使这些城市极其富庶，并且乐于接受新思想。例如，撒马尔罕在鼎盛时期成为中亚最大的城市之一，人口超过十万。

paragraphs.en: The Silk Road declined after the rise of sea routes, but its legacy never disappeared. Today, the spirit of the Silk Road continues in modern agreements like the Belt and Road Initiative. New trains now run from China to Europe, carrying electronic goods and clothing. Yet the ancient story still reminds us that trade is not merely a transaction; it is a conversation between cultures. The caravan is gone, but the exchange of ideas is stronger than ever. As one scholar put it, 'The Silk Road was the first international internet.' Indeed, the journeys of merchants and the goods they traded woven a web of connections that would shape the world for thousands of years. Even today, we see the marks of this ancient web in the world's shared tastes, technologies, and religions.
paragraphs.zh: 丝绸之路在海路兴起后逐渐衰落，但其遗产从未消失。今天，丝绸之路的精神延续到"一带一路"倡议等现代合作中。如今，新列车从中国开往欧洲，运送电子产品和服装。然而，这个古老的故事仍提醒我们，贸易不仅仅是交易，更是文化间的对话。商队已经消失，但思想交流比以往任何时候都更加强烈。正如一位学者所说："丝绸之路是第一个国际互联网。"的确，商人的旅程和他们交易的货物织成了一张联系之网，塑造了世界数千年。即使在今天，我们仍能在全球共同的品味、技术和宗教中看到这张古老网络的印记。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: The Silk Road was mainly a route for trading silk.
The Silk Road exchanged not only goods but also ideas and skills between East and West.
Roman glass was more valuable than Chinese silk on the Silk Road.
The Silk Road declined after sea routes became popular.
questions.explain: 文章主要讲述丝绸之路如何成为东西方商品、技术、思想交流的通道，而不仅仅是丝绸贸易。选项B正确；A过于片面，C错误（文中未比较两者价值），D只是末尾提到的内容。

questions.q: According to the passage, why was silk highly valued in ancient Rome?
options: Because it was difficult to weave.
Because it was used as currency.
Because it was weighed against gold.
Because it was rare and expensive.
questions.explain: 文中明确提到“silk was weighed against gold”，说明其价值与黄金相当，因此选C。A未提及，B未说作为货币，D虽是事实但不如C直接。

questions.q: What can be inferred about Chinese artisans before they saw Roman glass?
options: They already knew how to make clear glass.
They were unable to make clear glass.
They had no interest in glass.
They learned glassmaking from Rome earlier.
questions.explain: 文中说“the secret of making clear glass was unknown in China”，说明中国工匠当时不会制造透明玻璃，因此推断B正确。

questions.q: The word 'desolate' in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to:
questions.explain: 'desolate'意为“荒凉的”，由后文“with no villages for days”可知，选择A“空无一人的”。
